summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of FCNR deposits for NRIs, highlighting their benefits and features, though some specific claims about current interest rates and premature withdrawal penalties require careful consideration as they can vary significantly between banks and are subject to change.

claims.claim: Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) deposits currently offer attractive interest rates, ranging from 6% to 7.1%.
claims.note: Several banks are offering rates in this range for specific tenures, particularly for USD FCNR(B) deposits, especially due to a special RBI window until September 30, 2026.

claims.claim: The interest earned on FCNR deposits is entirely exempt from income tax in India for Non-Resident Indians.
claims.note: Interest earned on FCNR deposits is indeed tax-free in India for NRIs and Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) individuals.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) permits banks to offer FCNR deposits in a basket of freely convertible foreign currencies. These typically include the US Dollar (USD), British Pound Sterling (GBP), Euro (EUR), Japanese Yen (JPY), Australian Dollar (AUD), and Canadian Dollar (CAD).
claims.note: RBI guidelines confirm these currencies are typically accepted for FCNR(B) deposits.

claims.claim: The interest on FCNR deposits is usually compounded semi-annually, though the exact frequency can vary slightly between banks.
claims.note: RBI guidelines state that interest on FCNR(B) deposits is calculated and paid at intervals of 180 days (semi-annually), with an option for compounding at maturity.

claims.claim: The interest rates offered by banks are linked to international benchmark rates like LIBOR (London Interbank Offered Rate) or SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate), with banks allowed to add a spread within RBI guidelines.
claims.note: RBI guidelines confirm that FCNR(B) deposit interest rates are linked to international benchmark rates like LIBOR/SOFR, with banks allowed to add a spread.

claims.claim: FCNR deposits are bank deposits and are covered by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) up to ₹5 lakhs per depositor per bank, in case of bank failure. However, this coverage is in Indian Rupees, so for foreign currency deposits, the actual payout would be the Rupee equivalent up to the limit.
claims.note: DICGC covers FCNR deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, and the payout is in Indian Rupees.

claims.claim: Yes, premature withdrawal of FCNR deposits is generally allowed. However, banks may levy a penalty for early withdrawal, typically by reducing the interest rate paid on the deposit.
claims.note: Premature withdrawal is generally allowed, but banks typically have penalties, often involving a reduction in the interest rate or no interest if withdrawn before one year.

article_title: Why FCNR Deposits at 6-7.1% are Attractive for NRIs
